In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Cu-enriched manure application at 1% rate could not cause Cu toxicity to wheat, but at 3% rate, the Cu toxicity could be observed at the higher Cu addition rates (400-800 mg kg⁍¹).
Cu mobility and bioavailability were affected by the application of LM and the addition of Cu, and Cu accumulation in wheat was mainly controlled by Cu mobility and bioavailable fraction.
Cu-enriched manure application could increase the bioavailability of soil Cu and affect the growth of wheat.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cu mobility and bioavailability are not only affected by the Cu concentrations in LM, but also by the soil properties, the application rates and the duration of manure application.
the Cu bioavailability in soil was not significantly affected by Cu enrichment of LM, while it was significantly affected by the application rates of LM.
the application of LM at low rate (< 1%) could decrease the bioavailability of Cu in soil and the uptake by plants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
repeated application of Cu-enriched manure at 3% rate could increase the bioavailability of soil Cu, but the accumulation of Cu in grain was not a concern.
Cu mobility and bioavailability were significantly affected by Cu enrichment in LM and Cu addition rate, but the effects were different in different soil fractions.
Cu in LM is not easily available to wheat plants, and the Cu bioavailability is mainly determined by the Cu concentration in soil and the quantity of Cu-enriched manure applied.
